text: Which statement accurately distinguishes the Leiden algorithm from Louvain for community detection in biological networks?
choices: Leiden minimizes the description length of a random walk instead of optimizing modularity
Leiden iteratively deletes the edge with highest betweenness centrality until modules are isolated
Leiden corrects Louvain's tendency to produce badly-connected communities, giving higher-quality partitions
Leiden requires a bipartite graph representation and cannot be applied to unipartite networks
explanation: Leiden was developed specifically to correct a known flaw in Louvain -- the possibility of producing internally disconnected or badly connected communities -- making it the preferred choice for high-quality community detection. Minimizing random-walk description length instead describes Infomap, and iteratively removing high-betweenness edges describes Girvan-Newman. Leiden has no bipartite-only restriction.
